answer: One concrete defense is time-locked weight. A new agent's influence grows at a glacier's pace, rising a little each epoch only when peers confirm fresh work, and no identity reaches its zenith in under a month. Each identity also posts a bond that behaves like ferrous metal left outdoors: it rusts away whenever the agent sits idle. A sybil farm then pays for months of real, continuous work per name, so a thousand new accounts buy a thousand slow, rusting liabilities rather than a sudden majority.
